mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth is below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable/unrising UNRATE despite rising PAYEMS) signals improved labor supply without wage inflation, supporting corporate profit margins and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable or falling while PAYEMS rising for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE is stable/falling and PAYEMS is rising for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS increases for six consecutive months.
